summary_en: This study tests INBRX-106, a hexavalent OX40 agonist antibody, alone or with pembrolizumab, in people with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors, including lung, head and neck, melanoma, stomach, kidney and bladder cancers. Pembrolizumab is given by intravenous (IV) infusion, at 200 mg every 3 weeks or 400 mg every 6 weeks depending on the arm, and the route for INBRX-106 is not stated. The study aims to determine safety and identify the maximum tolerated dose or recommended Phase 2 dose, and the primary outcome measure is not stated.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa INBRX-106, un anticuerpo agonista de OX40 hexavalente, solo o con pembrolizumab, en personas con tumores sólidos localmente avanzados o metastásicos, incluidos cánceres de pulmón, cabeza y cuello, melanoma, estómago, riñón y vejiga. El pembrolizumab se administra por infusión intravenosa (IV), a 200 mg cada 3 semanas o 400 mg cada 6 semanas según el grupo, y la vía de administración de INBRX-106 no se indica. El estudio busca determinar la seguridad e identificar la dosis máxima tolerada o la dosis recomendada para fase 2, y la medida de resultado principal no se indica.
who_for: Locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors that progressed on standard therapy or have no standard option left.
Certain cancers in expansion cohorts, such as lung, melanoma, head and neck, stomach, kidney or bladder cancer, with PD-L1 criteria per protocol.
Previously untreated resectable Stage II to IIIB lung cancer, able to have planned surgery (one cohort).
Adequate blood, liver and kidney function and ECOG performance score as defined in the protocol.
not_for: Prior exposure to OX40 agonists or to anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L2 or other co-stimulatory pathway agents.
Hematologic malignancies such as leukemia, lymphoma or multiple myeloma.
Grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse events, or one that led to stopping prior immunotherapy.
Active autoimmune disease or history requiring systemic treatment.
History of hepatitis B, hepatitis C or HIV infection.
